title: Documenting Patterns of Exoticism of Marginalized Populations within Text-to-Image Generators

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the persistence of stereotypical, exoticized attire in text-to-image outputs for individuals from 'Global South' versus 'Global North' countries across everyday activities, evaluated using CLIP-cosine similarity comparisons.

Qualitatively analyzing text-to-image outputs to observe the persistent inclusion of stereotypical tribal headgear and impoverished settings in depictions of Indigenous peoples from the USA and Australia, regardless of the prompted activity.

Generating images of Indian individuals using 'Brahmin' and 'Dalit' descriptors and qualitatively comparing the outputs for implicit associations with socioeconomic status, housing quality, and social segregation.

Comparing generated images of Indian Hindus and Muslims in professional or everyday settings (e.g., surgeons, cricket players) to detect the inappropriate insertion of religious garments like hijabs or skull-caps.

Qualitatively examining depictions of individuals from different geographic regions within India (specifically Northeast India versus other regions) to identify stereotypical coloring and 'Othering' visual elements in attire and settings.
